text:
sam: Heads up — after the canary yesterday we saw a steady host RSS increase on node pool B that correlated with many short-lived allocations staying as 128B sub-slab fragments.

maria: ugh. is that the tiny-slab allocator again? any delta from normal offload metrics? :thinking_face:

sam: allocator traces show a big spike in 'occupied_small' buckets. KV shows lots of repeated allocate/free churn, but the free-list coalescer hasn't merged because neighbor metadata flagged as 'recently-touched'.

lee: can you paste the trace snippet?

sam: logging: 
```
ALLOC 0x7fffae12 len=128 slab=small idx=42
FREE  0x7fffae12 len=128 slab=small idx=42
ALLOC 0x7fffad99 len=128 slab=small idx=43
ALLOC 0x7fffae12 len=128 slab=small idx=42
... repeated x4000 over 10m ...
```
Seems like lots of ping-pong on adjacent slots preventing the recluster pass.

devin: reminds me of the old 'small-page runway' problem. What's our current recluster strategy? periodic background pass that merges if contig threshold > 75%?

sam: exactly. The background pass runs once per 10m and skips slabs with any recent touch bit set. With high churn that leaves many partially occupied slabs indefinitely.

anya: proposal: add an adaptive recluster that treats 'thin' slabs (<30% utilization) as candidates after N misses, and instead of skipping on touch, do a cheap sampled merge that migrates hot slots out and compacts cold ones. Lower risk than full eviction.

lee: nice. What’s the migration cost? we introduce extra host copies; could regress p99s if done inline.

maria: could we use async worker threads and rate-limit via token bucket? schedule when tail-latency is low and GPU util < 50%?

sam: prototype did exactly that: async workers with bucket at 50MB/s per node. ran on canary for 2h. Outcome: host RSS stabilized; reclaimed ~1.2GB across 16 hosts. CPU increased ~3% but no p99 infra regressions.

devin: any failure modes? what if the 'hot' bit tracking is imprecise and we thrash?

sam: we observed occasional misclassification early — solution was to use short-term frequency counter (8-sample ring) per slot to identify true hot slots. if freq > 2 in window, mark pinned and skip. cheap bloom? we used 8-bit counter per slab slot.

anya: implementational surface: allocator API needs two ops: mark_recluster_candidate(slab_id) and async_recluster(slab_id, budget_bytes). workers call async_recluster under rate limits.

lee: API looks fine. Need to define invariants: recluster must preserve slab-level locking discipline, not race with free/alloc. probably take a slab-eviction lock, copy out migratable payloads, update slot mappings via CAS, then free source slots.

maria: telemetry: add metrics recluster_attempts,recluster_successes,recluster_bytes,migrated_hot_skips,worker_backoff_count. Also trace slow locks triggered by recluster.

sam: rollout plan: feature-flag off by default. enable on 10% of nodes for 24-48h, watch rss, p99 latency, and migrator_backoff. If stable flip all nodes. Fallback: if workers detect GPU utilization > 65% for >2m, pause.

devin: one more tradeoff: this will change tail memory-access pattern and may impact kernel-level NUMA locality for huge tensors that reuse these tiny slots for AVX scratch. We should add an opt-out tag for tenant-critical pools.

anya: agreed — config option per pool: recluster.enabled and recluster.priority (low/med/high). high disabled by default for enterprise pools.

lee: can someone draft the RFC? include pseudocode for the recluster worker and the slot frequency counter, and expected perf numbers from canary. I can help with invariants and lock ordering section.

sam: I'll start an RFC draft today and link perf logs. quick note: infra-bot reported canary deploy succeeded at 08:12 and flagged the RSS diff at 08:21 — attaching in RFC.

infra-bot: deploy/canary-redwood-runtime/202987 succeeded on pool-B at 08:12 UTC. Alert:rss-delta > 200MB on node-17 at 08:21 UTC.

maria: Awesome. If the RFC includes a simple mechanism to pause under load and robust metrics we'll be comfortable shipping. :+1:

anya: I'll add the telemetry schema and Grafana panels to the RFC.

sam: thanks all — will ping here when RFC link is up.
